author: beaver state news
title: Mayor Wilson proclaims June and July 2026 as Pride Summer in Portland
text:
Mayor Keith Wilson proclaimed on June 24 that June and July 2026 will be recognized as Portland Pride Summer, encouraging all residents to honor, celebrate, and support the history, achievements, resilience, and future of LGBTQIA2S+ communities.
The proclamation states that the City of Portland remains committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, social justice, and mutual respect. It acknowledges the ongoing struggle of Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, Intersex, Asexual, Two-Spirit (LGBTQIA2S+) communities for dignity and equal rights. The document highlights the importance of honoring LGBTQIA2S+ movements’ history and centering marginalized voices such as transgender women of color Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera.
According to the proclamation text issued by Mayor Wilson’s office on June 24 in Portland City Hall chambers, “Pride is both a celebration and a call to action — honoring the generations who fought for equality while recommitting ourselves to building a future where all people can live openly, safely, and authentically.” The statement also recognizes that despite progress toward equality and inclusion in recent decades—reflected by over five decades of local Pride celebrations—LGBTQIA2S+ people continue facing discrimination and barriers including violence or limited access to housing or healthcare.
The proclamation notes that Portland has hosted Pride celebrations since 1971 with marches dating back to 1970. It further describes how LGBTQIA2S+ residents contribute daily across civic life—as artists, educators, or public servants—and references local organizations providing advocacy or services supporting youth through elders.
The statement outlines current challenges facing LGBTQIA2S+ individuals nationally such as efforts restricting gender-affirming healthcare or censoring stories about LGBTQIA2S+ experiences. It affirms an ongoing city commitment “to advancing policies…that affirm and support LGBTQIA2S+ residents” through continued action and investment.
Mayor Wilson concluded, “Now therefore I…do hereby proclaim June and July 2026 to be Portland Pride Summer in Portland.”

The document highlights the importance of honoring LGBTQIA2S+ movements’ history and centering marginalized voices such as transgender women of color Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera.
